classification.difficultyReason: Determine the transformed logarithm’s domain and shape, solve for its exact intercept, and place the intercept and asymptote consistently on the sketch.

content.prompt: Sketch the graph of each logarithmic function. Label the $x$- and $y$-intercepts wherever possible.

answer.worked: The logarithm is defined for $x>-2$. Its graph is increasing with vertical asymptote $x=-2$. For the $x$-intercept, $$\begin{align*}\ln(x+2)&=0\\x+2&=1\\x&=-1.\end{align*}$$ At $x=0$, $y=\ln 2$.

spec.description: Increasing curve, dashed vertical asymptote and both intercepts labelled.

answer.worked: The logarithm is defined for $x>0$, so there is no $y$-intercept. The graph increases from the vertical asymptote $x=0$. For the $x$-intercept, $$\begin{align*}2\ln(x)&=0\\\ln(x)&=0\\x&=1.\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Increasing logarithmic curve with the x-intercept marked 1.

answer.worked: The logarithm is defined for $x>0$, so there is no $y$-intercept. The graph increases from the vertical asymptote $x=0$. For the $x$-intercept, $$\begin{align*}3\ln(x)+2&=0\\3\ln(x)&=-2\\\ln(x)&=-\frac23\\x&=e^{-2/3}.\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Increasing logarithmic curve with the exact x-intercept marked.

answer.worked: Reflect $y=\ln(x)$ across the $x$-axis. The curve decreases and retains the domain $x>0$ and vertical asymptote $x=0$, so there is no $y$-intercept. For the $x$-intercept, $$\begin{align*}-\ln(x)&=0\\\ln(x)&=0\\x&=1.\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Decreasing logarithmic curve with the x-intercept marked 1.

answer.worked: Translate $y=-\ln(x)$ up by 2 units. The curve decreases and retains the domain $x>0$ and vertical asymptote $x=0$, so there is no $y$-intercept. For the $x$-intercept, $$\begin{align*}2-\ln(x)&=0\\\ln(x)&=2\\x&=e^2.\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Decreasing logarithmic curve with the exact x-intercept marked.

answer.worked: Translate $y=-\ln(x)$ down by 1 unit. The curve decreases and retains the domain $x>0$ and vertical asymptote $x=0$, so there is no $y$-intercept. For the $x$-intercept, $$\begin{align*}-1-\ln(x)&=0\\\ln(x)&=-1\\x&=e^{-1}.\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Decreasing logarithmic curve with the exact x-intercept marked.
